subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After authoritative write-time authorization is fixed, should plugin-runtime callers immediately fail closed on every legacy ownerless session row, or must an ownership migration be provided first?
rationale: Strict denial provides the strongest cross-plugin isolation, but it can strand legitimate persisted upgrade state created before `pluginOwnerId` existed; repository policy requires explicit ownership of that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Strict denial with recovery
options.body: Deny plugin-runtime patches on ownerless rows and document and prove operator or non-plugin recovery for those legacy sessions.

options.title: Add ownership migration
options.body: Provide a narrow doctor or operator adoption path for legitimate legacy rows before enabling strict runtime denial.

options.title: Temporary compatibility window
options.body: Permit ownerless plugin access under a named, time-bounded deprecation plan while accepting weaker isolation temporarily.

recommendation.title: Strict denial with recovery
recommendation.body: Deny plugin-runtime patches on ownerless rows and document and prove operator or non-plugin recovery for those legacy sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history connects this owner most directly to both the session projection boundary and the existing plugin ownership enforcement pattern.
